messages.text: Is the Magic Miner Harlo OS compatible?

Honest answer: I don't want to guess on firmware. Harlo OS is the Harlo line's software, and the 40T is a different manufacturer, so I've put that to our hardware guy rather than invent a yes.

Are you weighing the 40T against the B30?
Handed to the team · Firmware compatibility spec not in product facts; won't guess.

The team has it and will confirm by email — they pick it up today at 10am ET.

Meanwhile, the 40T at $799 does 40 TH/s at 650 W, so about $47 a month in power at 10¢ a kWh. What does electricity run you?
Weighing it against the B15 @ 14 cents Kwh
Ran the power-cost calculator · 14¢/kWh
Read the bsb b30 page
Searched the catalog · Harlo H15 Dual B30

Guessing you mean the H15 Dual — same $799, 15 TH/s Bitcoin plus 1.08 GH/s Scrypt, ~500 W, so $50 a month at 14¢. The 40T draws 650 W, $66 a month, but gives you 40 TH/s — nearly triple the Bitcoin hashrate and triple the block-shot.

If you want Dogecoin alongside, H15. If it's purely a Bitcoin lottery ticket and stacking sats, the 40T. Which is it?
Weigh it against the B30

Close call, same efficiency: 16.25 J/TH on the 40T, 16.2 J/TH on the B30 at Turbo.

40T: $799, 40 TH/s, 650 W, $66 a month at 14¢. B30: $899, 30 TH/s, 485 W, $49 a month — and it throttles down to ECO, 18 TH/s at 230 W, about $23.

More money for less hashrate on the B30, but it's the flexible one. The 40T is the better value per TH. Where will it sit — office or garage?
Turbo voids the warranty

Turbo is one of the three stock modes in the B30's own firmware — you pick it in the dashboard, same as Balanced or ECO. That's not overclocking. What voids the warranty is modifying or overclocking the unit beyond its stock modes.

If you want that in writing before you buy, I can get it confirmed with the hardware side.
The Magic Miner says it will void the warranty in turbo mode

Then take the page at its word — that's binding, and it's a real point in the B30's favour.

I've asked the hardware side to confirm both in writing: whether 40T Turbo voids it, and that B30 Turbo doesn't. You'll get that by email, and the team is on it from 10am ET.

If it matters to you, the B30 at $899 is the safer buy here.
Handed to the team · Warranty-vs-power-mode wording needs an authoritative answer before he buys.

That's with them now.

While you wait: do you want me to run the actual numbers at 14¢ for both — sats a month against the power cost, and the block odds per year — so you can see what the extra $100 buys you?
yes, run the numbers
Ran the power-cost calculator · 14¢/kWh

Here's the solid half, at 14¢:

40T — 40 TH/s, 650 W, 468 kWh a month, $65.52.
B30 Turbo — 30 TH/s, 485 W, 349 kWh, $48.89. Balanced 24 TH/s, $35.28. ECO 18 TH/s, $23.18.

Per dollar of power they're a dead heat — both give you about 0.61 TH for every dollar a month. So the extra $100 on the B30 doesn't buy efficiency; it buys the three modes and the warranty clarity.

On sats-per-month and block odds I'd rather give you the live figure than a stale one, so that's coming with the warranty answer. Honest note: at home power the sats usually come to less than the electricity — that's not why people buy it. You're buying a draw at a 3.125 BTC block every ten minutes, for years, on a machine you keep.
when is the next halving for BTC

Block 1,050,000, expected around spring 2028 — roughly April, though it drifts with block times. The reward goes from 3.125 BTC to 1.5625.

Worth knowing for the jackpot side: hit a block before then and it's 3.125 BTC. The machine keeps drawing after, just for half.

Does that change your lean between the two?
Seems like the wiser choice is the B30
Built a cart

I'd agree — the modes give you room to dial it to whatever your bill tolerates.

How do I register on Helium Deply website?

You don't need an account to buy — checkout takes your email and address as a guest, and the order confirmation comes to that email.

If you want one anyway, the account link is in the site header; you enter your email and it sends you a code, no password.

Anything else before you check out?
no ty
Used the chat-interview skill
Before you go, one thing: what made the warranty wording the thing you pushed on hardest?
I dont see a place to register

There isn't a sign-up form — that's why you can't find it. The account gets created with your first order, and after that the person icon in the header logs you in by emailed code, no password.

So just check out as normal and you'll have one.
